title: Tremor in Parkinson's Disease
content: Tremor can be a movement symptom of Parkinson's disease and is often an early symptom, but not everyone with Parkinson's develops tremor. A typical Parkinson's tremor commonly occurs at rest and may begin on one side of the body. It frequently affects the hands but can also involve other body areas. A resting tremor may become less noticeable when the affected body part is actively being used. Tremor by itself should not be treated as confirmation that someone has Parkinson's disease because shaking can have other causes.
